claim: In Envoy AI Gateway's AIGatewayRoute CRD, a BackendRef can reference either an AIServiceBackend or an InferencePool, but not both in the same rule, and only one InferencePool is allowed per rule.
stance_target: which backends belong behind the EPP vs beside it -- InferencePool and generic AIServiceBackend are mutually exclusive routing targets at the rule level
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway (Agent Router) v1.1 API, aigateway.envoyproxy.io/v1alpha1
quoted_support: BackendRefs can reference either AIServiceBackend resources (default) or InferencePool resources from the Gateway API Inference Extension. When referencing InferencePool resources: - Only one InferencePool backend is allowed per rule - Cannot mix InferencePool with AIServiceBackend references in the same rule

claim: When an AIGatewayRoute rule references an InferencePool, fallback behavior is entirely delegated to the InferencePool's own endpoint picker; the gateway's own backend-level priority and fallback fields are explicitly ignored for InferencePool backends.
stance_target: the EPP owns intra-pool failover logic; the gateway's own load-balancing controls do not apply inside an InferencePool-fronted pool
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway v1.1 API reference
quoted_support: Priority is the priority of the backend. This sets the priority on the underlying endpoints... Note: This will override the `faillback` property of the underlying Envoy Gateway Backend. This field is ignored when referencing InferencePool resources.

claim: For AIServiceBackend (non-InferencePool) references, fallback/failover across multiple backends is achieved by combining multiple AIServiceBackend entries with Envoy Gateway's BackendTrafficPolicy (failover and retry features), not via the InferencePool mechanism.
stance_target: how external/managed-provider backend fallback is implemented outside the EPP path
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway v1.1 API reference
quoted_support: For AIServiceBackend references, you can achieve fallback behavior by configuring multiple backends combined with the BackendTrafficPolicy of Envoy Gateway.

claim: As of the current API version, an AIServiceBackend's BackendRef must point to an Envoy Gateway Backend resource, not a bare Kubernetes Service; native k8s Service support is planned future work tracked in envoyproxy/ai-gateway issue #902.
stance_target: the claim that AIServiceBackend already supports arbitrary non-k8s or plain-Service backends today
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway v1.1 API reference
quoted_support: BackendRef is the reference to the Backend resource that this AIServiceBackend corresponds to. A backend must be a Backend resource of Envoy Gateway. Note that k8s Service will be supported as a backend in the future. See https://github.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/issues/902 for more details.

claim: BackendSecurityPolicy in Envoy AI Gateway supports authentication to external managed model providers via API key, AWS credentials (IAM/STS), Anthropic API key, Azure API key or Azure AD credentials (client secret or OIDC token exchange), GCP credentials, and generic OIDC.
stance_target: external-provider auth surface exposed by the gateway CRDs
scope_conditions: Envoy AI Gateway v1.1 API reference
quoted_support: BackendSecurityPolicy specifies configuration for authentication and authorization rules on the traffic exiting the gateway to the backend.
